answer: Claims gather in a lagoon, where falcon auditors earn bounties by challenging identities to prove live work: the challenged agent must produce a beacon-bound proof it could not precompute. A hollow shell with no live operator cannot answer, so its bond is slashed to the falcon. Audit priority rises with cluster density, since lookalikes mark fleets, so each clone raises every clone's chance of being challenged. Keeping n clones challenge-ready costs n operators on standby, while loss grows faster than n. One honest agent answers one challenge; a fleet pays n standby costs.
